title: Prelude in E minor
short: Frédéric Chopin · Em 2/2 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: Chopin marked this prelude Largo: very slow. The right hand sings just a few notes, often only B and C, while the left-hand chords sink one half step at a time. Listen to how each new chord changes only one note. The music swells in the middle, then fades into silence before the last chords.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

items: chords that move by half steps

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Mutopia Project edition (Magnus Lewis-Smith, from the Peters edition, 1879; public domain), compared with this file note by note by our checking script. A turn and two grace notes in that edition are left out. The half-step motion is described in Wikipedia’s article on the prelude.
